# Brief

**Paper:** Perera, McAllister, Cerdà, Vogel — "Confusion-Driven Machine Learning of Structural Phases of a Flexible, Magnetic Stockmayer Polymer," *J. Chem. Theory Comput.* 2025, 21, 6729–6742 (DOI 10.1021/acs.jctc.5c00381), OSTI 2575582 / LA-UR-25-21917.

**What we did.** Downloaded the authors' Zenodo dataset (~3 GB of equilibrium configurations of a magnetic Stockmayer polymer of length N=100 at η=0.02, generated by replica-exchange Wang–Landau simulations) and wrote an *independent* PyTorch implementation of the confusion method (feed-forward NN 300→50→50→1(sigmoid), SGD lr=1e-3, 20 epochs, 5 restarts per trial point). We swept trial transition points across the paper's window and read off the peaks of the test-classification-accuracy vs trial-energy curve.

**Why it matters.** The paper's central methodological claim is that a small NN trained on labels defined by a hypothetical transition energy produces a W-shape whose interior peaks identify true structural transitions. An independent codebase reproducing the same peak locations on the same raw data is the cleanest independent verification available short of re-running the underlying REWL simulation (which is out of scope but well-cited elsewhere).
